title: break: Exiting a Loop Early
learningObjectives: Explain break as an early loop exit.
Use search loops to stop at a match.
Understand break exits only the nearest loop.
Choose readable patterns for exiting nested work.

understand.concept: break exits the nearest enclosing loop immediately and continues after it. In nested loops it does not automatically exit outer loops.
understand.whyItMatters: Searches can stop as soon as a match is found, avoiding unnecessary checks.
understand.explain: Use break with a clear exit condition; use a flag or helper function for multi-loop exit intent.

examples.title: Inner loop break
examples.explanation: Break exits inner loop only; outer continues.

examples.title: Stop when sum reaches target
examples.explanation: Accumulation stops after reaching the threshold.

practise.guidedTask: For break: Exiting a Loop Early, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on break: Exiting a Loop Early. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.
